summary.intent: Get the Callisto 0.10.x release unblocked after the executor lost GH_TOKEN during attestation verification (E140), verify the fix end to end, then plan the next body of work for a fresh session.
summary.outcome: The gh credential fix (#199) was proven against the real gh, merged, and shipped in release 0.10.2 (all four crates, tags, GitHub release verified); 0.10.1 was never published. A NEXT-WORK.md plan doc was written and a PR opened.

repo: The executor's runner uses a keep-list of environment credentials per tool (`credentials_needed_by`); gh was missing GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, causing `gh attestation verify` to exit 4 in the release run.
Programs given by path are treated like their name when deciding which credentials to keep.
cargo publish goes through the plain runner, which keeps CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN; npm and PyPI publishers set credentials explicitly and don't depend on the keep-list.
The Release workflow can be recovered via workflow_dispatch with `release_source_sha`, which re-validates the commit is a GitHub-signed merge of exactly one managed release PR.
Release effects are idempotent, and re-runs adopt what already landed.
Merging a new changeset's release PR releases all pending changesets together, so 0.10.1 was skipped and versions jump from 0.10.0 to 0.10.2.
callisto-fixtures has publish = false and is intentionally not on crates.io.
The graph init.rs has template consts with placeholders (__BRANCH__, __COMMIT__, __VERSION__, __RELEASE_ENV__) and a roughly 1,300-line inline test module.
Release workflow changes since 0.10.0 were only dependabot bumps of taiki-e/install-action.
workflow: Reproduce production failures with the real tool through the real runner, not a fake; fake gh and fake cargo now refuse to run without their tokens so the harness catches credential regressions.
Check actual state (crates.io, tags, releases, Actions runs) before answering whether something published; the user's merge had triggered a different release than assumed.
Early PR state queries can race the merge; re-query before concluding a PR is unmerged.
Verify unconfirmed handoff facts against the repo before putting them in a plan doc.

friction: The first PR query showed #199 as open because it raced the merge.

The user's mid-session messages about the branding page logo, hero lede and tool columns didn't match any work in this session; the assistant found no matching page and the request was interrupted and rewound.
The assistant assumed 0.10.1 would be released, but merging the follow-up release PR shipped 0.10.2 instead.
A macOS-flaky broken-pipe test had to be fixed along the way.
open_items: Add a characterization test for the mixed-routing write steps in the apply.rs refactor (#196).
Add a CI check that runs the executor's `gh attestation verify` against the real latest release asset.
Confirm the #191 stale-read root cause on the next release PR refresh.
Clean up leftover stack/*, fix/* and refactor/* branches and the two worktrees under .claude/worktrees/.
Refresh ROAD-TO-V1.md and V1-FINDINGS.md, including which defects #177 closed.
Fix the SYS-RETRY, SYS-PYFILES, SYS-BARRIER and SYS-MATURIN product-safety defects; D01 gates part of them.
Qwen's debt: R1 (walk.rs), R3 (derive.rs, snapshots first), R5 (workflow templates and the graph init.rs test move), and the S1/S4/S5 decisions.
Decide whether Python dev-only dependency groups need tracking.
Decide whether distinct Cargo target-table declarations need graph edges, which requires a RewriteKey change.
The branding page logo (up 52px, left 12px), hero lede wrapping and heading styling requests were never addressed.
